answer:
Hold all the myriad details, documents and logbooks you need for your boats in one place, synched with the cloud. Fine tuned by personal use over several thousand miles underway.

The app enables you to create and manage:
• All the administrative details and documents for any of your boats.
• Equipment and Spares lists for each boat.
• A comprehensive Logbook recording the captain’s daily log, fuel log, pumpout log and GenSet log.
• Documents (files, photos, videos) can be attached to each boat, ships log, ships equipment, spare parts inventory, tools list, crew member, waypoint or ToDo item/note.
• Documents can be viewed, printed or shared.
• A database of recommended Planned Maintenance tasks and intervals, which can be added to a boat-specific Upkeep Logbook.
• Expiry Dates for documents (insurance policies), equipment (fire systems or PLBs) and spare parts (flares), each with an optional Calendar reminder.
• Crew lists with contact information, a default-crew flag, and a list of each log entry where the crew was aboard.
• Waypoints imported by GPX or CSV and selected in the logbook.
• Calendar and Map views of where you have been, with links to the relevant logbook entry.
• A popover dashboard (“the Helm”) showing where you are, the last log entry, upcoming dates for the default boat, and gauges for engine hours, fuel, water and holding tank.
• A popover ToDo list and Notes feature.
• The boat can have a Fuel Consumption data curve (least-squares fit) to estimate remaining fuel.
• Key statistics and charts: days underway, speeds, distances, costs, fuel consumption, plus a carbon-footprint estimate.
• Fully iCloud-enabled so your data syncs across devices—and still works offline, syncing when you reconnect.
• Apple Weather integration in logbook and Helm.
• Customizable links to tide and nautical-weather websites.
• Dark Mode for night-time use.
• CSV export of all your data (Numbers/Excel compatible) for backup or further analysis.

A personal project by a USCG-credentialed Master Mariner and ex-Royal Navy officer.

The Ships log allows you to register events and places in order to keep track of major events in the life of your boat.

• Location can be provided from the devices GPS or from the imported waypoints. Shows on Apple maps when entered.
• The engine hours at the end of the log, synched with the boats record and Helm/Dashboard, so you always have the latest engine hours showing.
• Distance run is estimated from the great circle distance between log GPS lat/Lon and the last log entry. It can, of course, be overwritten with the real distance run. I usually enter if from my chart plotter.

• The **Day Log** The Full ships log with one entry per day. The default shows the departure and arrival times. This can be hidden under Settings
• The **Fuel Log** A filtered list for any fuel entries, showing date, location, fuel quantity and cost.
• The **Pumpout Log** A filtered list for any pumpout entries, as required in some jurisdictions.
• The **GenSet Log** A filtered list for when the GenSet was run (if the boat has a GenSet)

The Distance Run is the distance you boat travelled that day.

It defaults to the Great Circle Distance between todays Port Latitude and Longitude and the previous Log Entries Latitude and Longitude.

Thats always and under estimate of the distance the boat travelled, so I usually type over it with the actual from my Chart Plotter.

The Distance Run shows on the log List.

Optionally the time of departure and arrival for the day can be used to calculate the Time elapsed. If you don't want these fields to show they can be turned off on the Settings screen.

The Hours underway defaults to whatever the difference between the departure and arrival times are, assuming they are on the same day. 

Hours underway is the not necessarily the same as Engine hours. It is hours underway that shows on the Log List. 

The RPM field is optional. I enter the average RPM for the day. It's used to estimate the fuel consumption.

SOG is Speed over the Ground. The Calculator button will divide the distance run by the hours underway. It is also used to estimate the fuel consumed.
